Queensland Cotton Corporation has been pivotal in the Australian cotton through their involvement and contribution locally, but also through supplying premium cotton to the world’s textile markets. Their reputation as a leading cotton corporation has remained true for decades. From cotton ginning, marketing through to warehousing and exporting, our client is trusted by farmers and customers across Australia to produce and supply superior and consistent quality cotton.

Your Role

We are currently seeking for experienced Mechanical Engineering Technicians to join our busy Cotton Ginning operations located in Emerald, Cecil Plains, Moura and Dalby, QLD. During the season, working on a shift roster, you will be involved in all aspects of ginning operations, including monitoring production, troubleshooting and repairing mechanical issues to improve Gin productivity. You will also be doing the preventative maintenance on Gin machinery and equipment.

You will be responsible for (but not be limited to):

* Performing Gin checks with the specifications and machines settings, to make sure the cotton gin running at optimal levels.
* Diagnosing and resolving breakdowns of ginning equipment promptly to ensure downtime is minimised.
* Monitoring downtime statistics and troubleshoot problems.
* Carrying out necessary repairs and maintenance per the agreed schedule.
* Changing or fitting hydraulic hoses.
* Review parts inventory.
* Help to maintain good plant hygiene and support general maintenance activities.
* Ensure safe systems of work and adhere to the company’s safety management system.

About you

To be considered for this position, you will need to prove the following:

* Mechanical trade qualification and certificate, or employment experience in lieu
* Minimum 2 years relevant work experience, ideally in cotton ginning.
* Previous maintenance and mechanical experience.
* Exposure to managing a diverse team or shift in remote or isolated environment.
* Reasonable computer skills, high levels of literacy to understand safety instructions and good communication skills to work effectively as part of a team.
* Understanding of hydraulic system.
* Knowledge of Australia’s work Health and Safety requirements is ideal.
* Fitness to be able to manage long shifts during the season.
* Great work ethic, eager to learn and able to think on your feet to troubleshoot.
* Respectful and able to interact with people from diverse cultures.
* Valid driver license.
* For the right candidate, the annual salary package of $80,000 - $95,000 + super is on offer.

About Us

Queensland Cotton Corporation has been going strong for 100 years, supplying premium cotton to the world's textile markets. We are a wholly owned subsidiary of Olam Agri, a leading global food and agri-business.

result.description: SDO  The Production Engineer is responsible for planning, developing and optimising manufacturing processes for the production of optical fibre current sensors, optical current transformers, transducers and related electrical monitoring equipment. The role focuses on improving manufacturing efficiency, product quality and production performance through engineering analysis, process optimisation and continuous improvement while ensuring compliance with engineering specifications, quality standards and workplace safety requirements.   Benefits   Task & responsibilities   Duties:    Plan and improve manufacturing processes for the production of optical fibre current sensors, current transformers, transducers and related electrical products.  Analyse production processes and identify opportunities to improve productivity, product quality and manufacturing efficiency.  Prepare and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs) and process specifications.  Coordinate production activities to ensure products are manufactured on time and meet quality standards.  Investigate production issues, equipment faults and product defects, and implement corrective actions.  Monitor production performance and recommend process improvements to enhance efficiency and reduce waste.  Support the introduction of new products through production trials, process validation and manufacturing implementation.  Evaluate manufacturing equipment and recommend upgrades or process improvements to improve production performance.  Ensure manufacturing activities comply with engineering specifications, quality standards, workplace health and safety requirements and relevant Australian standards.  Work closely with Engineering, Quality, Production and Supply Chain teams to support continuous improvement and achieve production objectives.    Responsibilities:    Ensure manufacturing processes operate efficiently and achieve production and quality targets.  Maintain accurate engineering and production documentation.  Provide technical support to production staff and assist in resolving manufacturing issues.  Monitor product quality and ensure compliance with engineering specifications and company standards.  Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and implement practical engineering solutions.  Support equipment commissioning, process validation and engineering change implementation.  Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) policies and company procedures.  Collaborate with internal teams to support production planning and timely customer delivery.     Qualification & experience   Bachelor's degree or higher in Production Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.  Minimum of one (1) year of relevant full-time work experience as a Production Engineer or in a similar manufacturing engineering role.  Knowledge of manufacturing processes, production planning and process improvement.  Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.  Understanding of quality management systems and workplace health and safety (WHS) requirements.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Good communication and teamwork skills.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with ERP/MRP systems or manufacturing software is an advantage.   About Company    Founded in Sydney in 2004, Smart Digital Optics (SDO) manufactures optical fibre current sensors for the electric power and smelting industries. Smart Digital Optics is one of the first companies to incorporate optical fibre current sensors into power monitoring and metering systems allowing users to measure electric currents with unprecedented levels of accuracy and ease. The digitally compatible and compact SDO products offer superior utility and performance compared to costly and cumbersome traditional approaches.  In 2010 SDO formed a strategic alliance with the Arteche Group. Arteche has 65 years of experience in the manufacture of electrical power products for generation, transmission, distribution and industrial applications. As an international benchmark with equipment in service in over 150 countries, it has companies in Europe, America, Asia and Oceania, as well as a service network comprised of more than 80 technical and sales offices.  The combination of SDO’s technology expertise with Arteche’s long experience in the electricity sector provides customers with a partner well equipped to support the introduce new technology for advanced transmission and industrial systems.   Technology :   SDO uses its expertise in advanced optics and signal processing to develop solutions for power engineering applications.  SDO’s optical current sensors utilize the Faraday effect in optical fibre, whereby the state of polarization of the light propagating in the fibre interacts with the magnetic field around a conductor.This effect is highly linear and provides the basis of an ultra high bandwidth, wide dynamic range current sensor which measures both AC and DC current with high accuracy.
